channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: US Dollar: Fading rallies as Fed pricing peaks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities' Macro Research’s FX team notes the softer US payrolls data is only marginally negative for the Dollar, with the labor market still described as buoyant and neither overheating nor deteriorating.

item.title: US Dollar: FOMC minutes to offer limited fresh clues – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities analysts characterize the upcoming September FOMC minutes as largely outdated given subsequent employment and PCE data. The minutes are expected to show disagreement over how much further tightening is needed, but broad consensus that policy should remain more restrictive.

item.title: Japanese Yen gives back post-NFP gains despite US Dollar weakness
item.description: USD/JPY trades around 157.65 on Friday at the time of writing, down 0.28% on the day. The pair briefly dropped to 156.95 following the release of the United States (US) employment report before erasing the entire move and returning to pre-release levels.

item.title: Canada labour market: Tariff effects assessed – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada analysts review Canada’s September labour report, the first full dataset since U.S. Section 338 tariffs took effect. They estimate around 0.4% of Canada’s GDP and employment is tied to tariff-listed US demand.

item.title: RBI to keep tightening risks alive – MUFG
item.description: MUFG analysts Lin Li, Michael Wan, Lloyd Chan and Khang Sek Lee highlight that Asia FX will be driven by the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) finely balanced decision on 7 October.

item.title: US labour market: Softer jobs ease Fed hike risk – ABN Amro
item.description: ABN Amro’s Rogier Quaedvlieg notes September US labour market data came in weaker than expected, with payrolls at 29k versus consensus 90k and prior months revised down by 60k. He see the report as mixed but consistent with its base case and reducing pressure for an October Fed hike.

item.title: Euro rebounds above 1.1250 after weak US jobs data weighs on US Dollar
item.description: EUR/USD rebounds to around 1.1260 on Friday, gaining 0.16% on the day at the time of writing, after hitting an intraday low of 1.1221 earlier in the day.

item.title: Euro: October ECB hike odds seen limited – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered Global Research team discusses Euro area monetary policy, noting that core inflation has only edged up slightly since January and that higher yields pose downside risks to both growth and inflation. The authors judge that these factors reduce the chances of an October rate hike and expect the Governing Council to wait for new macroeconomic projections at the December policy meeting.

item.title: Breaking: US Nonfarm Payrolls rise by 29K in September vs. 90K expected
item.description: Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) in the United States (US) rose by 29K in September, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported on Friday. This print followed the 133K increase recorded in August (revised from 162K) and missed the market expectation of 90K by a wide margin.

item.title: Euro hits fresh two-month lows against British Pound after hot Eurozone inflation data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) reverses previous daily gains against the British Pound (GBP) on Friday, diving to fresh two-and-a-half-month lows just above 0.8500, and is set to show a more than 1% weekly decline.

item.title: Australian Dollar trades higher against US Dollar ahead of US NFP data
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) is 0.17% higher at around 0.6640 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Friday. The Aussie pair gains as the Australian Dollar rises despite experts doubting about more Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) interest rate hikes.

item.title: Swiss Franc emerges as a safe-haven as global bonds sell off
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) is emerging as a safe haven amid the global government bonds sell-off, showing a surprising comeback against an otherwise firm US Dollar (USD) this week, as Switzerland's sound fiscal position stands out with government debt escalating amid the world's leading economies.

item.title: Euro: Downside risks despite ECB scope – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad reports EUR/USD has slightly recovered after hitting fresh cyclical lows, with support at 1.1200 and 1.1111.

item.title: Euro underperforms as France fiscal risks mount
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades lower against its major currency peers due to mounting fiscal worries in France. In the European trade, the major currency is down 0.35% at around 177.00 against the Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: France: Budget strains weigh on outlook – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad warns France’s budget crisis is deepening and complicating Eurozone fiscal dynamics. A minority government’s deficit-reduction plan faces parliamentary hurdles, while the fiscal watchdog calls assumptions optimistic.

item.title: Euro-area Inflation: Headline pressures rise – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Global Macro team of Tuuli Koivu, Jan von Gerich and Anders Svendsen note Euro-area inflation accelerated in September, driven mainly by energy and food.

item.title: US Dollar: Uptrend intact as NFP looms – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad notes the recent US Dollar rally and bond selloff have stalled as FOMC officials temper expectations for an October rate hike.

item.title: Mexican Peso: Carry liquidation pressures LatAm currencies – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny notes that rising rates volatility is driving a broader unwind of EM FX carry trades, with LatAm currencies under particular pressure. USD/MXN has surged and MXN long leveraged positions are being squeezed as implied volatility jumps.

item.title: Euro trims daily gains as Eurozone inflation accelerates above expectations
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is practically flat against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, with the EUR/USD pair trading at the mid-1.1200s, still close to the 16-month low of 1.1210 hit on Thursday.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $61.24 per troy ounce, up 0.43% from the $60.98 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: EUR/USD: French risk premium weighs on Euro – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner argues that the French debt sell-off has broken the narrative of ever-higher short-term rates and raised doubts about further European Central Bank (ECB) tightening.

item.title: Eurozone flash HICP rises faster by 3.8% YoY in September, beats 3.6% estimates
item.description: Eurozone’s preliminary Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) data for September arrives at 3.8% Year-on-Year (YoY), higher than 3.6% estimates and August’s final reading reading of 3.2%. On a monthly basis, inflationary pressures grew at a faster pace of 0.6% against the prior release of 0.4%.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Remains supported by 20-day EMA ahead of US NFP
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) trades higher against the US Dollar (USD) ahead of the United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for September, which will be published at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: Gold extends range play below $4,200; looks to US NFP for fresh impetus
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) steadies below the $4,200 mark during the first half of the European session on Friday as traders keenly await the release of US employment details.

item.title: S&P 500: Resilient as Fed tone turns dovish – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Early Morning Reid team reports that the S&P 500 broke a three-day losing streak, helped by a pullback in US Treasury yields and more dovish FOMC commentary. Despite strong US data and earlier upward pressure on yields, markets now price a much lower probability of an October Fed hike, supporting US equities into the upcoming jobs report.

item.title: British Pound holds near three-month lows, US Dollar shines as global yields surge
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) shows marginal gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, with the GBP/USD pair trading just above 1.3200, yet unable to take any significant distance from the four-week lows at 1.3180 hit on Thursday.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed pricing supports Dollar resilience – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes that the French debt sell-off triggered a reassessment of global rate expectations, but US short-dated yields only corrected modestly.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Safe-haven appeal strengthens – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister argues that rising global bond yields and mounting government debt concerns are increasingly supporting the Swiss Franc over the Euro. He notes Switzerland’s debt brake and relatively sound public finances as key advantages.

item.title: Australian Dollar flattens against Japanese Yen after Tokyo CPI data
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) turns flat at around 109.50 against the Japanese Yen (JPY) during the European trading session on Friday after recovering early losses.

item.title: ECB’s Rehn: Higher energy prices bring us closer to ECB’s adverse scenario for inflation
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) official and Finnish Central Bank Governor Olli Rehn said during the European trading session on Friday that elevated energy prices bring us closer to the central bank’s adverse scenario for inflation.
